thread:
anne_solutions: FYI AcmeCorp wants a committed capacity proposal for their POC. They expect ~120 req/s steady with 3x daily spikes to 360 req/s. They care about cost predictability and burst SLA.

Simon_infra: Thanks Anne. Do we know average prompt length / tokens per request? that'll change GPU sizing a lot.

anne_solutions: Rough estimate from their app team: 160 tokens in, ~80 tokens out on average -> ~240 tokens per request.

Jess_product: Quick calc: tokens/s = req/s * tokens/request. steady tokens/s = 120 * 240 = 28,800 t/s. spikes = 86,400 t/s.

Raj_sre: For an 8B-class model on our runtime, rough observed throughput per A100-80GB equiv with our batching is ~10k-15k t/s depending on seq len and batching. So steady would need ~3 GPUs, spikes ~6-9 GPUs.

Simon_infra: We should propose a reserved baseline of 4 GPUs (safety margin + KV cache warm state) with autoscale up to 10 GPUs for burst windows. That lets us hit 360 req/s with headroom.

Tom_salesops: How does that map to their commit? They asked for monthly committed units and a burst buffer.

Anne_solutions: Thinking: monthly commit = baseline capacity (4 GPUs * 24/7) + predictable buffer for scheduled spikes. Offer burst credits for autoscale usage above commit, billed at discounted overage rate.

Jess_product: Example calc we can share in the POC doc: 
```
Baseline: 4 GPUs reserved = 4 * 24 * 30 = 2880 GPU-hours/mo
Estimated burst: assume 3 hours/day of spike -> 3 * 30 * (10-4) = 540 extra GPU-hours/mo
Total commit proposal = 2880 GPU-hours + 540 = 3420 GPU-hours/mo
```

Raj_sre: Also call out cache warmup: when autoscaling up, cold-start tail latency can be higher until KV cache and kernels warm. Recommend warm standby policy for critical windows or pre-warm hooks.

Simon_infra: Agreed. Add canary routing: route 5-10% traffic to an inexpensive 4-bit quantized variant during load-shedding to preserve availability while saving GPU-hours.

Anne_solutions: Customer asked about SLAs for burst availability. Can we promise autoscale within X minutes?

Raj_sre: We can commit to scale-up within 2 minutes for Dedicated pools in same region if capacity available. If not, fallback plan is to degrade to quantized variant or route to hosted fallback model (higher latency but still up). Document that as part of the contract.

Tom_salesops: Pricing note: commit with 10% discount vs on-demand, burst credits at 40% of on-demand. Need to validate with finance, but that's the typical structure.

Anne_solutions: There's also a security ask: they want a filled security questionnaire and confirmation of KMS/HSM integration for keys and logs retention.

Jess_product: For Private deployment we can run inside their VPC and integrate with customer KMS. For Hosted/Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (KMS) and have SOC2 + audit logs. I'll attach standard sec questionnaire answers.

Simon_infra: Operational checklist for POC: run a 48h throughput test (sustained 120 req/s), a 2h stress at 360 req/s, and a failover test to quantized fallback. We'll capture latency and cost curves.

Raj_sre: Add health checks and circuit-breaker policies in the route: success_rate < 95% -> auto-failover, latency P95 > 1.5x target -> scale-up/invoke fallback.

Anne_solutions: Great. Action items: Simon to draft commit numbers & autoscale policy doc; Jess attach sec questionnaire; Raj define warm-standby & failover; Tom produce pricing example. I'll consolidate and send to AcmeCorp today.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: capacity-test-cluster will start at 2026-03-03T15:00Z (ETA 5m).

Anne_solutions: Thanks all — will loop in customer PM and set POC kickoff for next Tue. :thumbsup:
